name: Shima Kanko Hotel (志摩観光ホテル)

claims.text: Shared professional hotel kitchen; no gluten-free/celiac certification. Alternative dishes possible only by advance arrangement, so cross-contact control for celiac is not guaranteed.
Japanese fine-dining courses use standard soy sauce/miso (wheat/barley) unless specifically substituted — must be requested in advance.
「代替料理をご希望される場合はご予約時に承り、利用日の5日前までの申し込みが必要」— alternative dishes must be requested at booking, at least 5 days before arrival.
「ブッフェ形式のレストランや宴会につきましては原則としてアレルギーの情報提供のみ」— buffets/banquets provide allergy information only, no alternative dishes.
Formal group allergy policy: 8 designated allergens labeled on menus; 19 further items (except macadamia) provided on inquiry.

name: 大衆居酒屋 みしお (Taishu Izakaya Mishio)

claims.text: As a traditional seafood izakaya, sashimi and grilled dishes are served with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat. No wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned anywhere.
The menu centers on fish and shellfish, and broths/simmered dishes are very likely made with bonito (katsuo) or fish dashi; assume animal-derived stock throughout.

name: 鳥羽 海鮮料理 屋形船 おきた (Toba Kaisen Ryori Yakatabune Okita)

claims.text: The online booking form includes a remarks/notes section where customers can write health concerns for staff to respond to, but no allergen program or gluten-free/vegan accommodation is advertised.

name: 戸田家 コーヒーショップ (Todaya Coffee Shop)

claims.text: ブラックのホット／アイスコーヒー（各500円・税込）など、植物性ベースのドリンクが利用可能。

name: 和食堂 いせえび (Washokudo Iseebi)

claims.text: Signature fried items (jumbo shrimp fry, ebi-fry curry) use wheat-flour breading and would share fryer oil with other fried foods; no dedicated gluten-free fryer is indicated.
Sashimi and set meals are served with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat; no gluten-free/tamari alternative is mentioned.
The kitchen is entirely seafood-focused (lobster, abalone, fish, shrimp) and seasoned with fish-based dashi, so no vegan-safe separation exists.

name: 油そば 春日亭 渋谷店 (Abura-soba Kasugatei Shibuya Ten)

claims.text: The shop's signature tare is a secret blend of several soy sauces sourced from Kyushu, and the noodles are made with 100% Hokkaido wheat flour — a standard wheat-based soy-sauce noodle shop with no gluten-free noodle or sauce alternative identified.

The tare and stock base are built on chicken-bone (torigara) and pork-bone (tonkotsu) stock simmered for two days, so the standard dishes are not vegetarian or vegan; no plant-based broth or noodle option was found.

name: 穴子料理と地酒 浅草 川井 (Anago Ryōri to Jizake Asakusa Kawai (Asakusa)

claims.text: The menu explicitly includes tempura and fried preparations of anago alongside sashimi and grilled styles, indicating wheat-flour batter is used in the same kitchen.

name: アーンドラ・ダイニング 渋谷 (Andhra Dining Shibuya)

claims.text: A vegetarian version of the Andhra Meals thali is offered as a standard menu option alongside the non-vegetarian version, so vegetarians aren't limited to side dishes.
